angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 290,803 km at 23.78 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 42.0592 +/- 0.0324 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 23.78 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.418 +/- 0.029 solar radii from Zapatero Osorio et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-198 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.166Z/abstract): 290,803 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.417 +/- 0.045 solar masses from Zapatero Osorio et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-198 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.166Z/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3801 +/- 100 K from Zapatero Osorio et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-198 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.166Z/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Zapatero Osorio et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-198 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.166Z/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-198.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.816, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
